samples.summary: Board recovery feeds `applyImportedContent` read-back `Element`s where it expects mapper-minted `ElementInit`s, so every attached connector is silently dropped from the recovered copy
samples.evidence: New caller: `packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts:96` returns `{ type: 'board', elements: store.read().slides[0]?.elements ?? [] } as ImportedContent`. The out-of-diff consumer `applyBoardElements` (`apply-imported-content.ts:96-141`) builds `realIds` only from the mapper's private `__id` handle (`line 116: if (__id) realIds.set(__id, realId)`) and then remaps every connector endpoint through it (`line 126-131`): `remapEndpoint` returns `null` for an `attached` endpoint whose id is not in the map, and the connector is counted in `droppedConnectors` and skipped. Elements read back out of `YorkieBoardStore.read()` carry a real `id` and no `__id`, so `realIds` is empty and **every** attached connector in a recovered board is discarded. `recoverOfflineCopy` (`offline-copy-recovery.ts:~205`) also ignores the returned `ImportApplyResult.droppedConnectors`, so the outcome is reported with `complete: rebuilt.complete` and the user is told the copy is whole. This is the archive — by this feature's own design the only remaining copy of that work. The fix belongs on the new caller (remap ids, or pass through a board-aware writer).

samples.summary: `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` clears the remembered offline identity before the logout is known to have succeeded, leaving the still-signed-in session's purge call sites inert
samples.evidence: `offline-erase.ts:120` calls `rememberOfflineUser(undefined)` (clearing both module state and the `wafflebase-offline-user` localStorage mirror) unconditionally. `api/auth.ts:121-127` awaits it *before* the `if (res && !res.ok && !suppressFailure) throw new Error('Failed to log out')` check, so a logout the server refused still spends the identity while the user stays signed in. `OfflineRuntime`'s effect is keyed on `userId` (`components/offline-runtime.tsx:118`) and will not re-run, so for the rest of that session the out-of-diff consumers `purgeOfflineDocuments` (`api/documents.ts:166`, `api/documents.ts:214`) and `isOfflineUser` (`api/workspaces.ts:141`) read no user and silently skip their cleanup — deleted documents' local copies then linger until the thirty-day sweep, and self-removal from a workspace stops purging.

samples.summary: Every editor mount now joins the shared `['me','optional']` query, adding a `/auth/me` request per document open on private routes
samples.evidence: `collab-document-provider.tsx:181-188` adds `useQuery({ queryKey: ['me','optional'], queryFn: fetchMeOptional, retry: false, initialData: () => queryClient.getQueryData<User>(['me']) })` with no `staleTime`, so the seeded entry is stale on arrival and refetches. This cache entry is shared with out-of-diff observers that previously owned it alone — `PublicRoute.tsx:12`, `app/shared/shared-document.tsx:936`, `app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:213`, `app/docs/docs-view.tsx:193`, `app/home-or-redirect.tsx:13`, `app/home/marketing-page.tsx:35`, `app/templates/template-landing.tsx:80`. Previously no private-route editor (`docs-detail`, `slides-detail`, `board-detail`, `notes-detail`, `document-detail`, `files/pdf-collab`) issued this request at all; each document open now does one, and it is unconditional — it is not behind `supportsClientKey()`/the opt-in, so it costs a request even with the feature dark.

samples.summary: The background recovery offer fetches document titles through `fetchWithAuth`, whose 401 arm hard-redirects to /login as a side effect the local try/catch cannot suppress
samples.evidence: `offline-runtime.tsx:159-163` wraps `fetchDocument(described.id)` in a `try/catch` that only swallows the thrown value. `fetchDocument` goes through `fetchWithAuth`, whose 401 path (`api/auth.ts:245-257`) calls `logout({...})` and then `redirectTo('/login')` before throwing `AuthExpiredError` — a navigation the catch cannot undo. This runs on every authenticated mount of `PrivateRoute`, in a loop over archives, for a title that the comment itself says is 'a nicety'. A deleted-upstream document (one of the three archive-producing paths) that returns 401/403 through this helper therefore ejects the user from whatever page they were on.

samples.summary: `purgeDocument`'s suffix match can delete another document's local entry whose key ends with `-<id>`
samples.evidence: `wafflebase-doc-store.ts:~763-769` matches `docKey === documentId || docKey.endsWith('-' + documentId)`. It is driven from `purgeOfflineDocuments` (`lib/offline-erase.ts:~180`) with server-supplied ids reaching it from `api/documents.ts:166` (`deleteDocument`), `api/documents.ts:214` (`deleteDocuments`) and `api/workspaces.ts:117/145` (workspace delete / self-removal). Any stored document whose type-prefixed key ends with `-<deleted id>` — e.g. purging id `def` also matches `sheet-abc-def` — loses its local copy, including a non-empty change log the user could still push. Unlikely with full uuids, but the matcher is looser than the ids it is given.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `readContent`'s board branch (offline-copy-recovery.ts:91-101) feeds `applyImportedContent` elements read back out of `YorkieBoardStore.read()` (yorkie-board-store.ts:313-331), which are plain model `Element`s carrying a real `id` and no `__id`. The out-of-diff consumer `applyBoardElements` (apply-imported-content.ts:96-141) builds its `realIds` map exclusively from the Miro mapper's private `__id` handle (line 116), so on this path the map stays empty. `YorkieBoardStore.addElement` mints a fresh id and overwrites the incoming one (yorkie-board-store.ts:586, 623, 628), so archived connector endpoints (`kind: "attached"`, packages/slides/src/model/connector.ts:3-5) no longer resolve; `remapEndpoint` (apply-imported-content.ts:58-65) returns null and the connector is counted in `droppedConnectors` and skipped (lines 126-131). `recoverOfflineCopy` discards the returned `ImportApplyResult` (offline-copy-recovery.ts:211-213) and reports `complete: rebuilt.complete`, and offline-runtime.tsx:171-174 surfaces a clean "Recovered as ..." success. The path is reachable from the user-facing "Save a copy" toast action (offline-runtime.tsx:152-158) and `canRebuild` admits "board" (offline-copy-recovery.ts:50-58). This is a new caller reusing an out-of-diff consumer whose precondition (mapper-minted ElementInits carrying __id) it does not satisfy, causing silent loss of every attached connector in the only remaining copy of the work — a changed-contract/unupdated-consumer defect in the blast-radius lane, blocking at major.
